definition: a poor, crowded part of a city where housing is in bad condition

collocations.example: Many families live in the slum areas near the river.
The city announced a major slum clearance program last year.

definition: behaving in a clever and secretive way, often to deceive others

collocations.example: She gave a sly smile when no one noticed.
He threw a sly glance across the crowded room.

definition: a small or unexpected problem that makes something difficult

collocations.example: Our plans hit a snag when the funding fell through.
There is just one small snag with this proposal.

definition: an angry sound an animal makes while showing its teeth

collocations.example: The dog gave a vicious snarl at the stranger.
The cornered wolf backed away with a low snarl.

definition: to shoot at someone from a hidden position

collocations.example: Gunmen continued to snipe at troops near the border.
Rebels began to snipe at anyone crossing the square.

definition: to make a loud sound by forcing air through your nose

collocations.example: The children began to snort with laughter at the joke.
He snorted in disgust and walked out of the room.

definition: a sweet, fizzy drink; also plain carbonated water

collocations.example: She opened a cold can of soda after lunch.
He always orders a diet soda with his meal.

definition: to ask someone for money, support, or information

collocations.example: The charity hopes to solicit funds from local businesses.
Managers often solicit opinions from staff before deciding.

definition: having enough money to pay all your debts

collocations.example: The company struggled to remain solvent during the recession.
They worked hard to keep the business financially solvent.

definition: the quality of being advanced, complex, or highly developed

collocations.example: The software's technical sophistication impressed every engineer on the team.
Hackers attack with growing sophistication every single year.

definition: an object you keep to remember a place, person, or event

collocations.example: We bought postcards at the museum's souvenir shop.
She kept the ticket as a souvenir of the trip.

definition: existing in small amounts or spread thinly over an area

collocations.example: Only sparse vegetation grows on the dry mountain slopes.
The region has a sparse population and few towns.

definition: something unpleasant that people are afraid might happen

collocations.example: The layoffs raised the spectre of a long recession.
The whole region lives under the spectre of war.

definition: a small, thin, sharp piece broken off wood, glass, or similar

collocations.example: She got a splinter of wood in her finger.
The nurse used tweezers to remove the splinter.

definition: a soft material full of holes that soaks up water, used for cleaning

collocations.example: He wiped the table clean with a damp sponge.
She squeezed water from the soft bath sponge.

definition: a computer document that organizes numbers and data in rows and columns

collocations.example: She tracks the budget using a spreadsheet program.
Please enter the sales figures into the spreadsheet.

definition: a group of military aircraft, ships, or soldiers operating as a unit

collocations.example: A squadron of fighters flew over the city.
The squadron leader ordered the pilots to return.

definition: a short, high, thin sound

collocations.example: The mouse gave a tiny squeak of alarm.
The old door opened with a faint squeak.

definition: to look at something with your eyes partly closed

collocations.example: She squinted at the small print on the label.
He squinted in the bright afternoon sunlight.

definition: a small animal with a bushy tail that climbs trees and eats nuts

collocations.example: A gray squirrel buried acorns beneath the oak tree.
The flying squirrel glided between the tall trees.

definition: a basic or main food or product that people use regularly

collocations.example: Rice is a staple food across much of Asia.
Gossip is a staple of the tabloid newspapers.

definition: the respect and importance a person or thing has earned

collocations.example: The orchestra has grown in stature over the decade.
He is a man of great stature in science.

definition: a drug or natural substance that affects the body's hormones or reduces swelling

collocations.example: The athlete was banned for using an anabolic steroid.
The doctor gave him a steroid injection for the pain.

definition: a dish of meat and vegetables cooked slowly in liquid

collocations.example: She served a steaming bowl of beef stew.
They enjoyed a hearty stew on the cold evening.

definition: to stop something from happening or being expressed

collocations.example: She tried hard to stifle a yawn during the meeting.
Too many rules can stifle creativity in the workplace.

definition: to state clearly that something must be done, especially in an agreement

collocations.example: The rules stipulate that all staff must wear badges.
The contract stipulates a strict delivery deadline for suppliers.

definition: to bend the upper body forward and down

collocations.example: He had to stoop down to enter the low doorway.
She stooped to pick up the fallen papers.

definition: strong and thick; not easily broken or worn out

collocations.example: You will need stout shoes for the mountain trail.
He walked slowly with a stout wooden stick.

definition: a narrow channel of water connecting two larger areas of sea

collocations.example: Ships pass slowly through the narrow strait.
The strait between the islands is very deep.

definition: left somewhere with no way of leaving

collocations.example: Hundreds of stranded tourists waited at the closed airport.
The breakdown left us stranded on the motorway.

definition: to kill someone by pressing tightly on their throat

collocations.example: The attacker tried to strangle the shop owner.
He threatened to strangle the victim with a rope.

definition: to make a process or organization work more efficiently

collocations.example: The new software helped streamline the approval process.
The company streamlined operations to cut unnecessary costs.

definition: very strict and demanding; difficult to satisfy

collocations.example: The government imposed stringent controls on all imports.
The factory must meet stringent safety standards.

definition: strong and solidly built; not easily broken or knocked over

collocations.example: Use a sturdy ladder when you reach the roof.
The table's sturdy construction will last for many years.

definition: to divide something that is already divided into smaller parts

collocations.example: The teacher subdivided the class into small groups.
They subdivided the project into manageable stages.

definition: to bring someone or something under control, often using force

collocations.example: Troops were sent in to subdue the rebels.
Police struggled for hours to subdue the riot.

definition: to go below the surface of water, or put something under water

collocations.example: The submarine can submerge in water within minutes.
Floodwater rose to completely submerge the parked cars.

definition: to become gradually less strong or intense

collocations.example: We stayed indoors until the storm subsided.

collocations.collocation: wait for the pain to subside
collocations.example: She took a pill and waited for the pain to subside.

definition: to stay alive with only a small amount of food or money

collocations.example: Many families subsist on less than a dollar a day.
The refugees could barely subsist through the harsh winter.

definition: to secretly weaken or try to destroy a system or authority

collocations.example: They used bribes to subvert the entire legal system.
The pamphlets were designed to subvert state authority.

definition: to stop resisting something and give in to it

collocations.example: He finally succumbed to pressure and resigned.
She succumbed to temptation and ate the whole cake.

definition: to be enough for a particular purpose

collocations.example: Generally a brief note will suffice as a reply.
One example should suffice for our purposes here.

definition: to be better, greater, or stronger than someone or something else

collocations.example: Sales this quarter surpassed all our expectations.
The young runner surpassed the national record easily.

definition: so strange that it seems more like a dream than reality

collocations.example: Meeting my childhood idol was a surreal experience.
The empty city had a surreal, dreamlike atmosphere.

definition: a large group of insects moving together

collocations.example: A swarm of bees settled on the apple tree.
An angry swarm of wasps chased the picnickers away.

definition: to move or fly down suddenly and quickly

collocations.example: The eagle swooped down to catch the fish.
The hawk swooped on the unsuspecting field mouse.

definition: a unit of sound in a word containing one vowel sound

collocations.example: The stressed syllable in 'begin' is the second one.
You stress the first syllable in 'happiness'.

definition: a group of people or companies working together for a business purpose

collocations.example: They formed a syndicate to buy the racehorse.
The gang ran a powerful international crime syndicate.

definition: a word that means the same, or nearly the same, as another word

collocations.example: The word 'happy' is a synonym for 'glad'.
Can you give a synonym for this word?

definition: a thick, sweet liquid made with sugar

collocations.example: She poured maple syrup over the warm pancakes.
Boil the fruit gently in a light sugar syrup.

definition: the total amount of money you owe, for example in a bar or restaurant

collocations.example: Her boss offered to pick up the tab for dinner.
They ran up a large tab at the hotel bar.

definition: something that is forbidden or avoided because of social or cultural rules

collocations.example: Discussing salaries is still a social taboo here.
The film broke a long-standing cultural taboo.

definition: a record of a number of things, especially a continuing count

collocations.example: She kept a tally of the money she spent.
The scoreboard shows a running tally of the points.

definition: a ship or truck built to carry large amounts of liquid or gas

collocations.example: An oil tanker ran aground off the coast.
A tanker truck delivered fuel to the station.

definition: having a sharp, sour taste

collocations.example: The cranberries give the sauce a tart flavor.
These green apples are deliciously tart and crisp.

definition: a permanent picture or design made on the skin with ink

collocations.example: She decided to get a tattoo on her birthday.
He has a dragon tattoo on his arm.

definition: to say insulting things to someone to upset or provoke them

collocations.example: The older boys would taunt him about his accent.
Don't taunt the losing team after the match.

definition: a place where people go to buy and drink alcohol, like a bar or pub

collocations.example: They stopped for a drink at the local tavern.
The tired travelers rested at a small roadside tavern.

definition: the special words and expressions used in a particular subject or field

collocations.example: The manual is full of confusing technical terminology.
Always use the correct terminology in your report.

definition: a sharp, pointed growth on the stem of a plant

collocations.example: A sharp thorn pricked her finger as she gardened.
The ball disappeared into a dense thorn bush.

definition: to move or wave about in a violent, uncontrolled way

collocations.example: The patient began to thrash around in the bed.
The swimmer thrashed wildly against the strong current.

definition: to feel or make a strong, regular beat, especially from pain

collocations.example: His injured ankle began to throb with pain.
He could feel his pulse throb steadily in his wrist.

definition: to prevent someone from doing something or stop a plan from succeeding

collocations.example: Quick thinking by staff thwarted the robber's plan.
Security forces thwarted the attack at the last minute.

definition: to touch someone's body lightly in a way that makes them laugh or tingle

collocations.example: The older girls liked to tickle the small child.
The soft feather tickled the skin on her arm.

definition: one of several levels or rows arranged one above another

collocations.example: Only the top tier of players earns that much.
They removed an entire tier of middle management.

definition: to become unsteady and fall over, or to make something fall over

collocations.example: The tall stack of books began to topple over.
Protesters tried to topple the huge bronze statue.

definition: a force that causes rotation or twisting

collocations.example: This diesel engine produces impressive torque at low speeds.
The motor delivers high torque for heavy lifting.

definition: to praise or promote something strongly to persuade people to accept it

collocations.example: The drug was touted as a miracle cure.
Salespeople touted the benefits of the new phone.

definition: a poisonous substance, especially one produced by living things

collocations.example: The snake's venom contains a deadly toxin.
The illness is caused by a bacterial toxin.

definition: illegally bought, sold, or moved, especially people or drugs

collocations.example: The charity has rescued dozens of trafficked children.
Thousands of women are trafficked across borders every year.

definition: to write down in full what someone has said

collocations.example: It took hours to transcribe the long interview.
Court clerks must transcribe every word accurately.

definition: lasting only for a short time; not permanent

collocations.example: The medicine had only a transient effect on the pain.
The resort has a largely transient population in summer.

definition: things you throw away because they are no longer wanted; garbage

collocations.example: Would you please take out the trash tonight?
She dropped the wrapper into the trash can.

definition: to travel or move across or through an area

collocations.example: The camels slowly traversed the vast open desert.
The climbers had to traverse a dangerous glacier.

definition: behavior that betrays someone's trust; betrayal

collocations.example: Selling the plans was an act of treachery.
He was accused of political treachery by his party.

definition: a long, difficult journey made on foot

collocations.example: It was a long trek to the nearest village.
They set off on a trek through the mountains.

definition: a group of three people or things, especially closely connected ones

collocations.example: The novel explores a trinity of love, loss, and hope.
Debt, poverty, and crime formed an unholy trinity there.

definition: a basket or cart on wheels used for carrying goods, such as shopping

collocations.example: She filled her shopping trolley with fresh groceries.
He pushed the loaded trolley through the supermarket.

definition: to beat someone or something by having a greater advantage

collocations.example: Lower prices helped the firm trump the competition.
A rival buyer trumped our offer at the auction.

definition: an official given great power to deal with a particular problem or area

collocations.example: The president appointed a new drug tsar last week.
The government named an energy tsar to cut costs.

definition: a serious infectious disease that mainly affects the lungs

collocations.example: He contracted tuberculosis while working in the crowded camp.
The patient was treated for pulmonary tuberculosis.

definition: the money paid for being taught, especially at a college or university

collocations.example: Many students struggle to afford the rising tuition fees.
Her parents helped her pay tuition each semester.

definition: a large sea fish that is eaten as food

collocations.example: She opened a can of tuna for lunch.
He grilled a thick tuna steak for dinner.

definition: a machine that produces power using the movement of water, steam, air, or gas

collocations.example: A huge wind turbine turned slowly on the hill.
The power plant uses a giant steam turbine.

definition: a state of great confusion, uncertainty, or disorder

collocations.example: The whole country was thrown into political turmoil.
Her mind was in turmoil after the news.

definition: the soft, dim light in the sky after the sun sets

collocations.example: They walked home along the beach at twilight.
The hills slowly faded into the evening twilight.

definition: strong string made of twisted threads, used for tying things

collocations.example: She tied the parcel with a ball of twine.
He fastened the climbing plants with green garden twine.

definition: having two parts or aspects

collocations.example: The trip served a twofold purpose for the team.
The problem is twofold: cost and time.

definition: relating to light waves that are shorter than visible light and can harm skin

collocations.example: Too much ultraviolet light can damage your skin.
The ozone layer blocks harmful ultraviolet rays.

definition: an official who makes sure players follow the rules in sports like tennis or baseball

collocations.example: The players accepted the umpire's decision without complaint.
The baseball umpire called the runner out.

definition: to support or form the basis of something

collocations.example: Strong exports underpin the country's growing economy.
Years of careful research underpin this scientific theory.

definition: to say that something is smaller or less important than it really is

collocations.example: Officials tried to understate the problem to the press.
These figures greatly understate the true cost.

definition: already happening or in progress

collocations.example: The construction work will get underway next month.
An investigation is already underway into the crash.

definition: to accept financial responsibility for something, so that you pay if money is lost

collocations.example: The government agreed to underwrite the small business loan.
The firm will underwrite the new insurance policy.

definition: done by only one group or country, without the agreement of others

collocations.example: They were forced to take unilateral action.
The board criticized his unilateral decision to cut jobs.

definition: the state of doing or saying something together at the same time

collocations.example: The team members acted in unison to finish quickly.
The whole crowd shouted the answer in unison.
